assessments.summary: Measles cases in the US are peaking with a 100% increase from the same period last year, driven by a sharp rise in reported cases.
Dengue cases in the US are peaking with a 853% increase from the same period last year, indicating a significant surge in reported cases.
Mpox cases in the US are peaking with an 87% increase from the same period last year, though the number of cases has decreased from the previous year.
Influenza activity is peaking globally with a 27% increase in test positivity over the past month, and US hospitalizations are rising sharply.
Polio Wikipedia readership is at the 98th percentile of the past year, suggesting heightened public interest but no confirmed increase in cases.
West Nile virus cases in the US are peaking with a 1388% increase from the same period last year, indicating a sharp rise in reported cases.
Legionnaires' disease cases in the US are rising with a 45% increase from the same period last year, though the number of cases has decreased from the previous year.
RSV activity is at baseline with a 57% increase in hospitalizations over the past month, but global test positivity has decreased slightly.

Chikungunya cases in the US are at baseline with a score of 59/100, showing a slight increase in reported cases this year compared to last year. The first locally acquired cases were reported in Switzerland in October 2026.
US COVID-19 hospital admissions are at baseline with a score of 56/100, showing a 13% increase in hospitalizations over the past month compared to the previous month.
Pertussis cases in the US are rising with a score of 55/100, showing a 55% increase in reported cases over the past 8 months compared to last year.
Malaria cases in the US are at baseline with a score of 51/100, showing a 30% increase in reported cases over the past 8 months compared to last year.
Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) readership is at the 36th percentile of the past year, indicating a rising trend in public interest.
Hepatitis A cases in the US are at baseline with a score of 45/100, showing a 10% increase in reported cases over the past 8 months compared to last year.
Typhoid fever readership is at the 36th percentile of the past year, indicating stable public interest.
